title: Links under AppData leak inside the Claude and Codex apps
explanation: One cause of NTFS records (pool tag NtFC) piling up while the Claude or Codex desktop app runs: a bug in bindflt.sys, the filter behind a Store app's AppData. Each open through a junction or symbolic link under AppData, by the app or a program it starts (a terminal, git, Python, a hook), leaves one reparse-point record until a Restart. Opens by the real folder, through a link on another drive or under the profile (where Documents and OneDrive usually are), or from outside the app left none. A link inside OneDrive, and OneDrive's cloud files inside the apps, were not measured.
workaround: Reach the files without such a link: put the folder each PATH entry's link leads to in its place, and move uv, pnpm, the Codex command-line tool and Claude Code's temp folder out of AppData with their own variables, then reinstall what they hold. These measured 0 new records. Only a Restart frees what has built up: a Shut down with Fast Startup on keeps it.
suggestion: Opens through links under AppData leave these behind (traced by peterlau03 on GitHub). PoolWatch shows each link it finds and how to fix it.
